title: Mini surge liaison effort estimate and actions — May 2029
body:
Purpose:
Quick ad-hoc spreadsheet to size liaison effort for an anticipated short surge (estimated 72 hours over next 10 business days) so we can staff temporary coverage and escalate blockers. Not a final plan — meant to be lightweight input for product-ops, SRE, and solutions-eng leads.

Context / constraints:
- Spike: temporary traffic increase expected for a marketing pilot in region-eu-west starting ~2029-05-20.
- Objective: ensure no route-level SLO regressions during pilot; provide owner-level handoffs and minimal runbook.
- Timebox: 10 business days starting day-0. Use conservative estimates (padding +20%).

Quick summary metrics (back-of-envelope):
- Raw estimated liaison effort: 58 hrs
- Contingency buffer (+20%): 12 hrs
- Total planned liaison capacity to request: 70 hrs (~9 person-days)
- Priority bucket: P1 (routes with >99.5% read latency SLA impact) = 3 routes; P2 = 6 routes

Tracker columns (compact):
Liaison | Team | Estimated hrs | Priority | Current status | Blockers | Immediate next action
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Platform oncall | site-reliability | 18h | P1 | prepped, standby | none | allocate 2x 4h shifts (days 1,3) + slack
API gateway owner | infra/gateway | 8h | P1 | config review pending | rate-limit rule question (JIRA-7812) | finalize rule and test on staging (Ben)
Routing/Failover | serving-runtime | 10h | P1 | KV-cache tuning draft | needs perf test infra | schedule perf run (Trevor), fallback test (María)
Customer success liaison | customer-success | 6h | P2 | notified | no immediate blockers | prepare customer-facing template
Solutions engineering | solutions-eng | 6h | P2 | draft runbook | doc gaps for canary | write quick canary checklist
Observability lead | observability | 6h | P2 | dashboards queued | sampling rate needs change | deploy sampling tweak to staging
Dedicated capacity ops | dedicated | 5h | P2 | capacity reserved (soft) | billing owner assignment | confirm billing owner and hard reserve
Security review | security-and-compliance | 4h | P3 | queued | no major issues flagged | fast-path signoff for pilot
Console/Rollouts | product/console-and-rollouts | 3h | P3 | ready | none | schedule canary window
Incidents liaison backup | product-ops | 2h | P3 | standby | none | prepare escalation matrix

Notes on estimates:
- Estimates assume 4h shift granularity for oncall-like tasks; split between reactive and pre-launch prep.
- Platform oncall estimate includes 2 planned warm-up shifts + 2 ad-hoc slots for surge days.
- Serving-runtime routing work assumes a single perf engineer + one ops runner. If perf infra unavailable, escalate to infra team (increases hours).

Actionables & asks (short):
- Ben Wu: finish rate-limit rule review + attach test commands to JIRA-7812 (due 2029-05-13).
- Trevor Lin: book perf test slot and run KV-cache perf test (due 2029-05-15).
- María González: produce canary checklist and customer template drafts (due 2029-05-16).
- Aisha (me): request temporary headcount (70 hrs) from product-ops and confirm billing contact; set daily 15m standup for the sprint window.

Risks & mitigations (quick):
- Risk: perf infra queue delays -> mitigation: fallback to smaller synthetic perf runs + increase contingency; notify incubator team early.
- Risk: billing/commit delay for dedicated reserve -> mitigation: soft-reserve and request manual cap increase for pilot window.
- Risk: unexpected error mode in region -> mitigation: pre-authorize cross-region fallback and ensure cross-region routing tests are in place.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we require SLA exception for pilot if traffic > projected? (ask legal/security)
- Can solutions-eng provide an extra engineer for day-2 if perf tests show >30% degradation?

Notes to self / working scratch: 
- If fluctuation looks low on day-1, reassign 6h from platform oncall to serving-runtime tuning.
- Consider short-lived synthetic load generator run the night before pilot (2h setup + 3h run).

Versioning / history:
- v0.1 2029-05-11: initial draft and estimates (Aisha)
- v0.2 2029-05-13: updated after Ben + Trevor quick sync (reduced routing estimate by 2h)
- v0.3 2029-05-14: added contingency + final action owners; moving to in_review

Appendix (quick links):
- JIRA-7812 (rate-limit rule)
- Confluence: Mini Surge Plan (link above)
- Perf infra queue: https://internal-tools.redwood/perf-queue

Unresolved shorthand notes:
- "fallback-spray" refers to temporary cross-region fallback mapping (we need to map to owned routes list)
- "KV-cold" callouts were from 2028-11 incident postmortem; reuse checklist there

End of tracker.
